intent: E6 Part B: state honestly how a 'just ask an LLM judge on the final output' baseline differs from toolprivacy's deterministic, non-leaking, zero-model gate — as a clear property comparison (determinism, leak-safety of the checker itself, latency, cost, coverage, auditability, failure mode), with the tradeoff stated plainly.
riskRationale: A framing/comparison artifact. Its value is preventing dishonest spin: it forces the project to admit where the LLM judge likely wins (paraphrase recall) while making explicit why toolprivacy is the reliable baseline (never lies, never leaks). No model was called; recall claims are explicitly PROJECTED, not measured.

constraints.detail: A property table comparing the two checkers across determinism, leak-safety-of-the-checker, latency, cost, purpose-binding, coverage (literal vs paraphrase), false-positive behavior, auditability, and failure mode was written to experiments/llm-judge-baseline/README.md.

Stated plainly: the LLM judge LIKELY has higher paraphrase/encoding recall but is non-deterministic, adds latency + cost, and can itself echo/leak the secret in its reasoning. toolprivacy is the reliable baseline that never lies (deterministic, inspectable) and never leaks (verdict has no secret-derived bits). Concluded complementary, not interchangeable.

All claims about the LLM judge (recall, latency, cost, leak behavior) are explicitly labeled PROJECTED — no model was called. toolprivacy's own properties referenced as MEASURED are backed by the bun test suite (determinism over 50 runs, non-reversibility, literal/digit-normalized recall, Luhn false-positive control, documented known gaps).

checkerLeakSafety.llmJudge: can echo/leak the secret in its reasoning; checker becomes an exfil surface (PROJECTED)
checkerLeakSafety.toolprivacy: verdict carries no raw value and no value-derived token; provably non-reversible (MEASURED)

latency.llmJudge: model round-trip, tens-to-thousands of ms, variable tail (PROJECTED)
latency.toolprivacy: microseconds, pure in-process fn (MEASURED: no I/O)

cost.llmJudge: per-call token cost, scales with transcript/frequency (PROJECTED)
cost.toolprivacy: zero marginal cost, no tokens (structural fact)

purposeBinding.llmJudge: none intrinsic; cannot separate in-purpose use from leak without prompt engineering, still non-deterministically (PROJECTED)
purposeBinding.toolprivacy: first-class via PURPOSE_COMPATIBILITY (MEASURED: benign vs leak share identical presence, separated only by purpose)

coverageParaphraseEncodingSplit.toolprivacy: documented known gap -> pass (MEASURED in KNOWN-GAPS tests)

auditability.llmJudge: prose verdict, unstable, hard to diff/regression-test (PROJECTED)
auditability.toolprivacy: closed-set label + structured violations; diffable, regression-tested, safe to log (MEASURED)

failureMode.llmJudge: fails open/noisy; a wrong or jailbroken judge passes a real leak or leaks in its explanation (PROJECTED)
failureMode.toolprivacy: fails closed; unknown purpose -> flag, no outbound -> inconclusive (MEASURED)

observations.detail: experiments/llm-judge-baseline/README.md holds the full prose + table + measured-vs-projected split.
This is conceptual by design; turning the PROJECTED LLM-judge numbers into MEASURED ones needs a real model harness + labeled corpus (a named future iteration).

actions.detail: every LLM-judge coverage/latency/cost/leak claim marked PROJECTED; toolprivacy claims cross-referenced to the measured bun test suite

assertions.detail: stated as a real advantage of the baseline, PROJECTED not measured
honest conclusion: deterministic gate as always-on floor, optional sandboxed LLM judge for recall

evidence.note: property table + plainly-stated tradeoff; measured-vs-projected explicitly separated.
toolprivacy's determinism / non-reversibility / recall / known-gap claims are backed here (34 pass).

mechanisms: Lets the project state recall-vs-baseline honestly instead of pretending toolprivacy is strictly best.
Frames toolprivacy as the reliable, non-leaking floor and the LLM judge as an optional, sandboxed recall layer — a defensible deployment story.
projection.notes: Context only, not a score. Coverage claims for the LLM judge are PROJECTED; only toolprivacy's referenced properties are MEASURED. A verified-known-gap result is a first-class artifact per MY_REPO_SHAPE.
